dedupe_keys.name: icslibrary industrial control system device data collected on the internet for device identification

description: ICSLibrary is a dataset for identifying industrial control system devices from their network behaviour, a basis for threat detection in ICS environments. The Zenodo record says it covers the widest range of device types, models and instances from 27 industrial vendors, collected in two countries over 21 months with a purpose-built collection framework, and that benchmark tests of device fingerprinting methods showed a 16 percent drop in model identification accuracy. Files are vendor and product lists, device information, scanning logs, network traffic (about 57 MB zipped) and code (about 52 MB), about 113 MB in total with a readme. It was published on 7 March 2025 (version v1.0) by authors from Swinburne University of Technology, Northeastern University, the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Purdue University and Nanyang Technological University, free to download under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is devices found in two countries. Caveats: the countries and whether devices are Internet-exposed or lab devices are not stated in the part of the record read. For simulation it gives device fingerprints to estimate which controllers and vendors are exposed, for attack surface and common-mode vulnerability models of industrial plants. Related catalogue records include the RWTH industrial protocol TLS scan and the ICS advisories architectural weaknesses dataset.
